findings.claim: Removing this branch means that when a user configures only `toNotFake` (leaving `toFake` undefined), `nextTick` and `queueMicrotask` are now faked, since `@sinonjs/fake-timers` fakes every supported method by default and only `toNotFake` is excluded.
findings.rationale: The first branch only sets the safe default when BOTH options are undefined. Previously the deleted `else if` preserved the same "don't mock Node internals" guarantee for users who passed `toNotFake`. After this change, `fakeTimers: { toNotFake: ['setTimeout'] }` silently starts mocking `process.nextTick`/`queueMicrotask`, which is exactly what the surrounding comment warns against and can deadlock/​break Vitest's own async internals. This is a real behavior change for existing callers; if intentional it deserves a changelog/docs note, otherwise it is a regression. Fairly confident about the mechanism (it follows directly from sinon's default-fake-everything semantics), less sure whether it was deliberate.

findings.claim: The child-process guard only re-adds `nextTick` and only when `toNotFake` is already truthy, so with the previous branch gone the child-process path can still end up faking `queueMicrotask` (and faking `nextTick` when the user passes only `toFake`).
findings.rationale: `toNotFake && !toNotFake.includes('nextTick')` is a no-op when `toNotFake` is undefined, and it never protects `queueMicrotask`. Before the change the deleted branch covered `queueMicrotask` for the `toNotFake`-only case; now that safety net is gone in child processes too. Worth double-checking whether this guard should be broadened to `toNotFake = [...(toNotFake ?? []), 'nextTick', 'queueMicrotask']`. Moderate confidence — part of this (the `toFake`-only case) is pre-existing, but the change widens the exposure.
